A mountain country of Central Asia, independent since September 1991, much of it high in the Pamir Mountains. The map shows it in 1994 and 2010.

Unlike their Turkic neighbours, Tajiks speak a form of Persian. They look back to the Samanids, the Persian dynasty of Bukhara, as their founders, and the national currency, the somoni, is named after the Samanid ruler Ismail Samani.

Independence brought disaster. From 1992 to 1997 the Tajik Civil War set the old Soviet-era elite against an alliance of Islamists and democrats, killing tens of thousands and driving many more from their homes. Emomali Rahmon came to power in 1992 and has ruled ever since; a peace deal in 1997 ended the war.

Tajikistan is the poorest of the former Soviet republics. Many men work in Russia, and the money they send home makes up a large part of the economy. Its rivers drive hydropower, including the giant Rogun Dam. The capital, Dushanbe, grew from a village in Soviet times.
